title: Sriram Dang v. State of U.P. And Others
coram: Sheo Kumar Singh, J.; Ram Surat Ram (Maurya), J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; petitioner may apply afresh; any such application to be considered under clause 4.4.
headnote: A writ seeking to quash rejection of a fresh electricity connection, alleged to have been withheld because of a landlord dispute, was disposed of without a merits grant or refusal. The petitioner may make a fresh application with all requisites; if made, the respondents shall consider it in accordance with clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Sriram Dang filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court seeking certiorari to quash an order dated 23 May 2012 rejecting his application for a fresh electricity connection, and a mandamus directing the respondents to grant the connection. He alleged that supply was being withheld because of a dispute with his landlord. The respondents submitted that he had not applied after completing the necessary formalities and that no connection could therefore be given.

holding_units.holding: The Court did not quash the 23 May 2012 rejection or mandamus a connection. It left it open to the petitioner to make a fresh application with all requisites, and directed that if made, the respondents shall consider it in accordance with clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Whether the 23 May 2012 rejection was lawful, and whether a landlord dispute barred a fresh connection
not_decided.note: Writ disposed by relegating the petitioner to a fresh application under clause 4.4; no finding on the alleged rejection or the landlord dispute.
